safeDescription: Follow these golden rules to stay safe online

kyc.name: KYC Update Scam
kyc.howItWorks: Scammers call/SMS claiming your KYC is expired. They send fake links that look like bank/government websites. When you enter details, they steal your credentials and empty your account.
redFlags: A link in a message asking you to verify KYC urgently
Asking for OTP, PIN, or CVV
prevention: NEVER click links in SMS for KYC
Visit bank branch or official website directly
KYC updates are FREE - never pay for it
Bank will never ask for OTP to update KYC
Verify by calling bank on official number
kyc.action: If scammed: Call 1930 immediately, then contact bank to freeze account. File complaint at cybercrime.gov.in as soon as possible.

anydesk.name: Remote Access Scam
anydesk.howItWorks: Scammer poses as bank/tech support. Claims your account is compromised. Asks you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or QuickSupport. Once they access your screen, they see your banking details and transfer money.
redFlags: Call asking to install remote software
Claiming to be from bank/SBI/HDFC/tech support
Asking you to open banking websites
prevention: NEVER install AnyDesk/TeamViewer on anyone's advice
Bank employees NEVER call to ask this
Never share screen with strangers
Hang up immediately if asked to install software
If installed, uninstall immediately and change all passwords
anydesk.action: If scammed: Uninstall remote app immediately. Disconnect internet. Call 1930 and bank. Change all passwords from a different device.

digital-arrest.name: Digital Arrest Scam
digital-arrest.howItWorks: Scammer poses as CBI/Police/Customs officer. Claims you're involved in money laundering/drug racket. Asks you to join video call, "verify" by showing ID, and transfer money to "verification account". Can last for days/weeks.
redFlags: No government agency asks for money via video call
Asking to keep it "secret" from family
Threatening immediate arrest if you don't comply
prevention: Police/CBI/ED NEVER call for digital arrest
No govt agency asks for money transfer
Never share video call with "officers"
End the call and verify the claim using an independently sourced official number
Tell family immediately - scammers isolate victims
digital-arrest.action: If scammed: Call 1930 immediately. This is a MAJOR crime. File FIR at local police station. Contact bank to reverse transactions.

upi-pin.name: UPI PIN Scam
upi-pin.howItWorks: Scammer says they'll SEND you money. Asks you to scan QR code or enter UPI PIN to "receive" payment. In reality, entering PIN authorizes money going OUT of your account.
redFlags: Asking for UPI PIN to RECEIVE money
QR code scanning to get payment
Any request for PIN when receiving money
prevention: UPI PIN is ONLY for SENDING money
NEVER enter PIN to receive payment
To receive: only share UPI ID/phone number
Verify recipient name before entering PIN
No bank/officer ever asks for UPI PIN
upi-pin.action: If scammed: Call 1930 as soon as possible. Contact bank. File complaint on cybercrime.gov.in. Check if money can be reversed via NPCI.

lottery.name: Lottery/Prize Scam
lottery.howItWorks: You receive email/call claiming you won a lottery (KBC, international lottery, etc.). To claim prize, you must pay "processing fee", "tax", or "customs duty". After payment, more demands come. You never receive any prize.
redFlags: You won a lottery you never entered
Asking for upfront fee to claim prize
prevention: Real lotteries NEVER ask for fees
If you didn't buy a ticket, you can't win
KBC and similar shows have official processes
International lotteries are ILLEGAL in India
Delete such emails immediately
lottery.action: If you paid: report at cybercrime.gov.in and contact your bank immediately.

sim-swap.name: SIM Swap Scam
sim-swap.howItWorks: Scammer tricks telecom operator into transferring your number to their SIM. They receive all your OTPs and take over bank accounts, crypto wallets, and other 2FA-protected accounts.
redFlags: Notifications of SIM change you didn't request
prevention: Set SIM lock PIN with telecom operator
Never share OTP with anyone
Use authenticator apps instead of SMS 2FA
Monitor account activity regularly
Contact telecom immediately if network drops
sim-swap.action: If scammed: Call telecom operator IMMEDIATELY. Contact bank to freeze accounts. File police complaint. Change all passwords.

fake-customer.name: Fake Customer Care
fake-customer.howItWorks: Google search shows fake customer care numbers for banks, Amazon, Flipkart, etc. When you call, scammer poses as executive, asks for details/OTP, and empties your account.
redFlags: Numbers found via Google (not official website)
Promising instant refund after sharing details
prevention: ONLY use numbers from official websites/apps
Bank numbers are on the back of your card
Customer care NEVER asks for OTP/PIN/CVV
Bookmark official customer care pages
Verify number before calling
fake-customer.action: If scammed: Call 1930. Contact official bank customer care. File cybercrime complaint. Report fake number to Google.

investment.name: Fake Investment Scam
investment.howItWorks: Fake trading apps/platforms promise guaranteed high returns (10-30% monthly). Show fake profits on app. When you try to withdraw, they ask for "tax" or "fees". Eventually, the app disappears with your money.
redFlags: Apps not on Play Store/App Store
Pressure to invest more to "unlock" profits
prevention: Check SEBI registration before investing
No investment guarantees 10%+ monthly
Only use registered brokers (Zerodha, Groww, etc.)
Research company thoroughly before investing
If it sounds too good, it IS a scam
investment.action: If scammed: Report to SEBI (scores.gov.in). File FIR with Economic Offences Wing. Report at cybercrime.gov.in. Contact bank.

job.name: Job/Work-from-Home Scam
job.howItWorks: Fake job offers for data entry, typing work, or "like YouTube videos". Ask for "registration fee" or "security deposit". After payment, either no work comes or impossible tasks are given. Money is never refunded.
redFlags: Asking for money to get a job
No company website or physical address
prevention: Real jobs NEVER ask for money
Verify company on LinkedIn/official website
Check reviews on Glassdoor/Indeed
Never pay "registration" or "training" fees
Be wary of unsolicited job offers
job.action: If scammed: File complaint at cybercrime.gov.in. Report on LinkedIn. Contact bank for chargeback if paid by card.

loan-app.name: Illegal Loan App
loan-app.howItWorks: Fake loan apps offer instant loans without documentation. They access your contacts/photos. When you default, they harass you and your contacts with morphed photos, threats, and humiliation. Interest rates are 300%+ annually.
redFlags: Apps not on official Play Store
Hidden charges and extremely high interest
prevention: Verify the lender through its official channels
Check app permissions before installing
Read terms carefully - look for hidden fees
Verify lender on RBI website
Avoid apps with <10,000 downloads
loan-app.action: If you are threatened, preserve evidence and contact the local police or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

qr-code.name: QR Code Payment Scam
qr-code.howItWorks: A scammer poses as a buyer and sends a QR code, saying to scan it to receive money. Confirming a payment request may send money from your account. Someone may also replace a shop’s QR sticker to redirect payments.
redFlags: QR code to RECEIVE money (never needed)
Buyer sending QR instead of scanning yours
prevention: To receive money: only share UPI ID/number
NEVER scan QR to receive payment
Verify QR code at shops before scanning
Check merchant name before entering PIN
Use official payment apps only
qr-code.action: If scammed: Call 1930 immediately. Contact bank. File cybercrime complaint. Report to UPI app provider.

matrimonial.name: Matrimonial Scam
matrimonial.howItWorks: Fake profiles on matrimonial sites. Build emotional connection over weeks. Then create emergency (medical, visa, business) and ask for money. Once money is sent, profile disappears.
prevention: Never send money to online matches
Verify identity through video calls
Meet in public places before sharing details
Check profile on multiple platforms
Inform family about online relationships
matrimonial.action: If scammed: Report on matrimonial site. File FIR. Cybercrime complaint. Preserve all chat records as evidence.

delivery.name: Fake Delivery/Customs Scam
delivery.howItWorks: SMS/email about package stuck at customs. Fake link asks for "customs duty" or "delivery fee". Payment goes to scammer. Or fake delivery person asks for OTP to "verify" delivery.
redFlags: Links in SMS for customs payment
Payment requests to personal UPI IDs
prevention: Track packages only on official courier sites
Customs duty is paid at official counters only
Never share a banking OTP with a courier
Verify sender before paying anything
Check tracking on official websites
delivery.action: If scammed: Contact courier company. File cybercrime complaint. Report to payment platform. File police complaint.

crypto.name: Crypto/Forex Scam
crypto.howItWorks: Fake crypto exchanges or "mentors" on Telegram/YouTube promise huge returns. Show fake profits. When you try to withdraw, they demand "tax" or "fees". Crypto is hard to trace and recover.
redFlags: An exchange whose identity you cannot independently verify
Requests to send crypto to "verify" wallet
prevention: Independently verify the exchange and understand the risks
No one can guarantee crypto profits
Crypto trading is risky - do your research
Beware of "pump and dump" schemes
Never share private keys with anyone
crypto.action: If scammed: Report to exchange. File cybercrime complaint. Note: Crypto recovery is difficult - prevention is key.

otp-phishing.name: OTP Phishing
otp-phishing.howItWorks: Scammer calls claiming to be from bank/OTP verification. Asks you to share OTP received on phone. Uses OTP to authorize transactions, change passwords, or take over accounts.
redFlags: Calls claiming to verify your identity
prevention: NEVER share OTP with ANYONE
OTP is like your password - keep it secret
Bank will never ask for OTP
If in doubt, hang up and call official number
Enable OTP via app instead of SMS where possible
otp-phishing.action: If shared OTP: Call bank IMMEDIATELY. Freeze account. Call 1930. Change all passwords. File cybercrime complaint.

learnIntro: Practise with fictional examples and see what to check before you act.
learnNoResults: No exercises match. Try QR, payment, or bank.
learnQrTitle: A buyer sends you a QR code
learnQrMessage: Scan this QR code to receive your payment.
learnQrWarning: Be cautious when a buyer asks you to scan their code to receive money. You do not need to enter a UPI PIN to receive a payment.
learnQrQuestion: How would you verify the payment?
learnQrSafe: Open my own UPI app and check my transaction history.
learnQrRisky: Scan the buyer’s QR code and enter my UPI PIN.
learnQrCorrect: Correct. Check for an incoming payment in your own app before handing over the item.
learnQrRetry: Try again. Entering your PIN to confirm a payment can send money from your account.
learnBankWarningLead: The real domain in this example is
learnBankWarningTail: The bank-like part is a subdomain. Check the complete address before trusting a link.
learnBankQuestion: How would you open your bank safely?
learnBankRisky: Use the link because the address contains the bank’s name.
learnBankSafe: Open my bank’s official app or use an address I verified with the bank.
learnBankCorrect: Correct. Use a route you already trust. A familiar name in a link cannot verify who runs the website.
learnBankRetry: Try again. A familiar name in an address can be placed before a different domain.
learnReport: Already lost money? Open Report Crime

collect.title: Unexpected UPI request
collect.sample: A stranger sends a collect request and says approval will release your refund.
collect.safe: Decline the request and verify the refund in the official app.
collect.risky: Approve the request to unlock the refund.
collect.lesson: Approving a collect request can send money from your account.

cashback.title: Cashback that asks for a fee
cashback.sample: A message promises a reward after you make a small payment.
cashback.safe: Check the offer inside the official app.
cashback.risky: Pay the fee to claim the reward.
cashback.lesson: A promised reward is no reason to pay a stranger or enter your PIN.

receipt.title: A buyer shares a payment screenshot
receipt.sample: The buyer shows a receipt, but your app has no matching incoming transaction.
receipt.safe: Check your own transaction history before handing over the item.
receipt.risky: Accept the screenshot as proof and hand over the item.
receipt.lesson: A screenshot can be edited. Confirm the payment independently.

sticker.title: A shop QR sticker looks replaced
sticker.sample: A sticker is pasted over the payment code at a shop counter.
sticker.safe: Ask the shopkeeper to confirm the payee and check the name before paying.
sticker.risky: Pay as soon as any name appears on screen.
sticker.lesson: A replaced sticker can redirect the payment. Check the payee and amount.

refund.title: A refund agent asks for card details
refund.sample: A caller says they need your card PIN and security code to process a refund.
refund.safe: End the call and contact the merchant through its official app.
refund.risky: Read out your card PIN and security code.
refund.lesson: Refund promises can be used to collect payment credentials. Keep your PIN private.

kyc.title: A text threatens to block your bank account
kyc.sample: The message says your KYC has expired and demands an immediate update through a link.
kyc.safe: Open your bank’s official app or call a verified bank number.
kyc.risky: Open the message link and fill in whatever it asks for.
kyc.lesson: A deadline and an unverified link are reasons to check the request independently.

family.title: A relative texts from a new number
family.sample: The sender claims to be your relative, asks for money, and says not to call.
family.safe: Call the relative on their known number before paying.
family.risky: Send money quickly because the message sounds urgent.
family.lesson: An urgent message is not identity verification. Use a contact you already trust.

parcel.title: An unexpected delivery fee
parcel.sample: A text claims your parcel is held and demands a small fee through an unknown link.
parcel.safe: Check tracking using the courier’s official site or app.
parcel.risky: Pay using the link before the parcel is returned.
parcel.lesson: Look up the parcel independently and confirm any fee with the courier.

attach.title: An invoice attachment you weren’t expecting
attach.sample: An unfamiliar sender urges you to open an attached invoice today.
attach.safe: Confirm with the supposed sender using a known contact.
attach.risky: Open the attachment to discover what the invoice is for.
attach.lesson: Unexpected attachments can contain harmful files. Verify before opening.

otp.title: A caller asks for an OTP
otp.sample: Someone claiming to be from the bank asks you to read the code on your phone.
otp.safe: Keep the OTP private and call the bank using its official number.
otp.risky: Read out the OTP to prove your identity.
otp.lesson: A code can approve a transaction or login. Never share it with an unsolicited caller.

arrest.title: A video caller claims you are under arrest
arrest.sample: A caller in uniform tells you to stay on video and transfer money for verification.
arrest.safe: End the call and independently contact the relevant authority.
arrest.risky: Stay on the call and pay to clear the case.
arrest.lesson: Threats and demands for money are warning signs. Verify through an official number you find independently.

electric.title: A message threatens to cut your power
electric.sample: A stranger says your electricity will be disconnected unless you pay using their link.
electric.safe: Check your bill directly with your electricity provider.
electric.risky: Use the message link to stop the disconnection.
electric.lesson: Check the bill in a channel you already know instead of following an unexpected link.

subsidy.title: An unexpected government benefit
subsidy.sample: A message promises a subsidy if you share your Aadhaar OTP.
subsidy.safe: Check the scheme through its official portal without sharing the OTP.
subsidy.risky: Send the OTP so the subsidy can be released.
subsidy.lesson: An unsolicited request for an Aadhaar OTP may put your information at risk.

customs.title: A caller demands a customs payment
customs.sample: A caller claims a parcel in your name is detained and asks for payment to a personal account.
customs.safe: Verify through official courier or authority channels first.
customs.risky: Transfer the money to the account the caller gives you.
customs.lesson: An accusation plus a personal payment request warrants independent verification.

job.title: A recruiter charges a registration fee
job.sample: A recruiter promises a guaranteed interview after you pay a personal account.
job.safe: Find the vacancy through the employer’s official careers page.
job.risky: Pay the registration fee before you lose the interview slot.
job.lesson: Verify the employer and vacancy before paying or sharing documents.

tasks.title: A task group demands a larger deposit
tasks.sample: A group pays for a small online task, then asks for a deposit to unlock bigger earnings.
tasks.safe: Stop paying and verify the business independently.
tasks.risky: Send a bigger deposit because the first task paid out.
tasks.lesson: An early payout can build trust. It does not establish that a later deposit is safe.

invest.title: A group guarantees high investment returns
invest.sample: A messaging group claims to represent a registered adviser and guarantees profits.
invest.safe: Verify the intermediary independently before acting.
invest.risky: Transfer money based on the group’s screenshots.
invest.lesson: A name or registration claim in a chat is not verification. Check through official channels.

loan.title: A loan app wants access to your contacts
loan.sample: An unfamiliar lender asks for contacts and photos to release a loan.
loan.safe: Verify the lender and stop if the permissions are unnecessary.
loan.risky: Allow all permissions to speed up the loan.
loan.lesson: Check that the lender is genuine and that access is necessary before sharing data.

prize.title: An unexpected prize requires a fee
prize.sample: A caller says you won a contest you did not enter and asks for a processing fee.
prize.safe: Verify with the organiser through an official channel.
prize.risky: Pay the fee to claim the prize.
prize.lesson: Unsolicited prizes and advance fees are a warning sign. Do not pay based on the call.

remote.title: A support agent wants to control your screen
remote.sample: A caller asks you to install a screen-sharing app and open your banking app.
remote.safe: End the call and contact support through its official channel.
remote.risky: Grant screen access while entering your banking details.
remote.lesson: Remote access can expose what you do and type. Verify independently before granting it.

apk.title: A message offers an app update file
apk.sample: A message asks you to install a file to continue using a service.
apk.safe: Update through the official store or trusted system updater.
apk.risky: Install the file sent in the message.
apk.lesson: An unsolicited installer can be unsafe. Use a trusted update route.

sim.title: Phone service disappears after a SIM-change message
sim.sample: You stop receiving calls after a SIM-change notification you did not request.
sim.safe: Contact your mobile operator through a verified channel from another phone.
sim.risky: Wait and give any caller your account codes to restore service.
sim.lesson: Ask your operator to check for an unauthorised SIM change and check for suspicious account activity.

backup.title: A pop-up offers to repair all your files
backup.sample: A pop-up demands that you install software to restore files.
backup.safe: Close it and use your trusted backup or support tools.
backup.risky: Install the repair tool from the pop-up.
backup.lesson: Verify the problem and use a backup you control. Avoid software offered through unfamiliar pop-ups.

account.title: You entered a password on a suspicious page
account.sample: You realise the page was not the service’s real sign-in page.
account.safe: Use a trusted device and the official service to secure the account.
account.risky: Return to the suspicious page and ask for help.
account.lesson: Change the exposed password through the official service and follow its account recovery steps.

loss.title: Money has already left your account
loss.sample: You find a transaction you did not authorise after interacting with a stranger.
loss.safe: Contact your bank through its official channel and open Report Crime for reporting information.
loss.risky: Wait for the stranger to promise a refund.
loss.lesson: Prompt reporting is important. Keep the transaction reference and communications.

evidence.title: A caller asks you to delete your chat history
evidence.sample: You are told a refund depends on removing messages and receipts.
evidence.safe: Keep the messages and transaction records for official reporting.
evidence.risky: Delete the records so the refund can go through.
evidence.lesson: Records can help you explain what happened. Share evidence only through trusted official channels.
